cards.#1: The AVANT Tour is the most expensive piece in the drop and, deliberately, the least camouflaged: Warm White and Birch with the Legacy pattern held back to the trim. It is a spiked tour shoe that reads as a dress shoe until you turn it over.
cards.#2: The HELSINKI G takes the opposite approach, running full Legacy across the whole upper of PUMA’s retro-running silhouette. It is spikeless, and it lands at $130 against the AVANT’s $190. It is also the best-looking object in the collection and the one piece that works entirely off the course.
cards.#3: The vest is full-pattern fleece with a shawl-ish collar and a yellow Realtree tab at the chest. It translates a hunting layer into a golf one more literally than anything else PUMA made here. At $140 it also sits at the top of the apparel range.
cards.#4: The hoodie is colour-blocked rather than fully patterned, with a Dusty Olive or Alpine Snow body and the Legacy print kept to the hood and sleeves. CLOUDSPUN is PUMA’s soft-handle knit, which makes this the comfortable one in the range. At $110 it sits in the middle of the apparel pricing.
cards.#5: The camo polo puts head-to-toe Legacy on a standard PUMA golf polo, and at $90 it is the piece the collection is really selling. Whether you want to stand on a first tee in full bark pattern is the entire question the drop is asking. Everything else in the range is a way of answering it more quietly.
cards.#6: The solid polo is for the people whose answer to that question is no. It comes in Dusty Olive or Warm White with the pattern confined to a collar tip and a woven tab, which makes it the $85 version you can wear to a members’ club.
cards.#7: The shorts run an eight-inch inseam in full Legacy, at $88. They pair with the solid polo if you want the pattern working on one half of you only, which is how PUMA styles them in nearly every lookbook image. That is the most usable version of the collection.
cards.#8: The performance tee is the cheapest way in at $55 and the only piece carrying the Realtree antler logo at scale. It comes in Alpine Snow or Dusty Olive with no pattern on it at all, which makes it a co-brand tee rather than a camo one.
cards.#9: The Tour cap carries a full Legacy crown across the whole panel, with the PUMA wordmark picked out in yellow. Forty dollars is the lowest-commitment way to try the pattern, which is presumably the point. It is also the cheapest fully patterned piece PUMA made for the drop.
cards.#10: The Precision cap is the rope-style alternative at the same $40, with an Alpine Snow crown, a Legacy brim and a woven PUMA GOLF patch. It keeps the pattern below the eyeline rather than above it. It is the more restrained of the two caps and the one that will date better.

kickers.1: Two shoes state the collection’s split personality as plainly as it gets: one hides the Legacy pattern in its trim, the other wears it across the entire upper. Sixty dollars separates them.
kickers.2: Three of these run fully patterned and three keep Legacy to the trim. PUMA has built the range so you can take as much or as little of the camo as you want.
kickers.3: Caps are the entry point at $40 each, and historically the hat is the piece of any camo collaboration that actually sells through. PUMA made two, one loud and one quiet.
